Primary witness: k = 3, n = 6. Here lcm(1,2,3) = 6, so the hypothesis n >= lcm(1,...,k) holds (with equality, i.e. at the boundary). pi(3) = 2, so the claim asserts that the interval [n, n+k] = [6, 9] contains at least k+1-pi(k) = 3+1-2 = 2 integers having a prime factor p > k = 3. Factorizations: 6 = 2*3 (no prime factor > 3), 7 = 7 (YES), 8 = 2^3 (no), 9 = 3^2 (no). So exactly ONE integer of [6,9] has a prime factor > 3. Claim says count >= 2; here count = 1 < 2. CLAIM FAILS.
